sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Post-merge setup steps
sections.what: Moves to the project root, points the Python environment to a managed folder, installs the locked Python packages with uv, installs the frontend packages with npm ci, builds the frontend, and creates the build folder. A note states that saved job data must never be changed here.
sections.why: Likely reason: a merge can change dependencies and the frontend, and this brings them up to date in the hosting environment. The build folder is needed by the test setup.
sections.watch_out: The note says saved job data must never be touched, so any new cleanup step added here must avoid job folders.

summary: A setup script that installs the Python and frontend dependencies, builds the frontend, and makes the build folder, so the project is ready after a merge.
purpose: Brings the project environment back in line after code changes arrive from a merge.
why: Likely reason: after a merge, dependencies or the frontend may be out of date, so the script refreshes them automatically. The comment says the saved job data must not be touched.
how: It moves to the project root, points the Python environment at a managed folder, and installs locked Python dependencies with uv. It then installs the frontend packages with npm ci and builds the frontend. Last, it creates the build folder that the test runner needs.
inputs: The project files, the locked dependency files, and the frontend folder.
outputs: A populated Python environment in .pythonlibs, a built frontend, and a build folder.
risks: It stops on the first error because of the strict shell settings. It is written for the Replit hosting environment, so its paths may not fit other machines.
debug: Read the last failing command in the output. Check that uv and npm are installed, and confirm the frontend folder exists.
